sections.h2: How can you sell a house in Stonecrest, Georgia?
sections.html:
Stonecrest owners have the usual three routes: an agent listing, a sale handled by the owner, or a cash offer from a buyer who purchases the house in its current state. Which one fits depends on repairs, mortgage balance, how soon you need to close and whether the house is occupied.

  • A listing works when the house is presentable and you can wait for a buyer's financing.
  • A for-sale-by-owner sale cuts out the agent but leaves pricing, disclosures and negotiation to you.
  • A cash offer is worth pricing out when the house needs work, carries back taxes or belongs to an estate.

Stonecrest sits inside DeKalb County, so county tax rules and county offices apply to every sale here, along with the city's own permit and licensing desk.

sections.h2: What is Stonecrest, and how new is the city?
sections.html:
Stonecrest is among the youngest cities in Georgia. Voters approved incorporation in a referendum on November 8, 2016, and the city began operating on July 10, 2017, according to its 2020 annual financial report. That report calls it the sixteenth largest city in the state as of 2020 and describes a mostly residential community of about 29 square miles.

The city runs planning and zoning, code enforcement, business licenses, and building permits and inspections. Police and fire protection, along with street maintenance and sanitation, were left with DeKalb County during the transition, and the report says the county continues to provide public safety. A mayor and five council members lead the government, with council seats elected by district. The first millage rate the city levied was set in 2020. Ask the DeKalb Tax Commissioner how any city levy appears on your bill.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about Stonecrest housing?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimates 61,337 residents on July 1, 2025, a 3.6 percent rise from the April 2020 base. The household count is 20,995 and the owner-occupied rate is 56.3 percent.

Median rent of $1,601 is the number a landlord-minded buyer uses to judge a house. The 36 minute commute is long, which fits the city's own description of itself as a bedroom community.

sections.h2: What makes Stonecrest different from other DeKalb County addresses?
sections.html:
The city's 2020 report names the Mall at Stonecrest as the commercial hub, ringed by medical, office and hotel parcels, with DeKalb Medical Center at Hillandale as the main hospital. It also identifies two industrial areas that host some of the biggest local employers, including Dart Container and Home Chef.

The outdoor side is just as distinctive. The Arabia Mountain National Heritage Area covers 2,550 acres of exposed granite, wetlands, streams, lakes and forest, linked by a trail network, and the Davidson-Arabia Mountain Nature Park and Panola Mountain State Park add to that. The city's tourism page points to the historic Flatrock community and to African American history and arts as parts of its visitor story.

For a seller, these places are selling points. A house near the heritage area trails or close to the mall corridor can be described by its distance to them, and a buyer who works at the industrial parks may value a short drive.

sections.h2: When are DeKalb County property taxes due, and who pays at closing?
sections.html:
DeKalb mails property tax bills in August to the owner of record on January 1, with a copy to the current owner when the two differ. Taxes can be paid in two installments, September 30 and November 15, or in one payment by September 30. A 5 percent penalty applies if the envelope is not postmarked by the date, and the county says metered or kiosk postage does not count as proof.

If the deed changed after January 1, the DeKalb Tax Commissioner says the new owner should check with the closing attorney, mortgage company, escrow agent or the closing statement to learn who owes the bill. Unpaid taxes keep accruing against the property. The county does not send bills to mortgage companies, so a seller whose lender pays from escrow should still confirm that the payment went out.

The single-family sanitation assessment on the DeKalb bill is printed on the county's page as $362.30 a year, and it is charged for trash pickup.

sections.h2: How do DeKalb homestead exemptions and appeals work?
sections.html:
A homestead exemption in DeKalb requires that you own and occupy the home as your primary residence on January 1, hold a Georgia driver's license or ID showing that address, and register your vehicles in the county at that address. The county's brochure lists the filing deadline as mid-July and adds that exemptions are not automatic and cannot be transferred to a buyer. A granted exemption puts an assessment freeze on county taxes, which may limit an increase, and the freeze does not reach school, city or state taxes.

  • Special exemptions are income-based and cover seniors aged 62 and over, disabled residents, 100 percent disabled veterans and certain surviving spouses.
  • An appeal of the notice of assessment has to be filed within 45 days, and appeals sent by fax or email are not accepted.
  • The three routes are the Board of Equalization at no charge, nonbinding arbitration with a $217 filing fee and a certified appraisal, or a hearing officer, limited to non-homestead property over $500,000.
  • If an appeal is still open when bills go out, the county bills at a temporary value, generally the lesser of the last final value or 85 percent of the current value.

Property is appraised at 100 percent of fair market value and assessed at 40 percent. The Property Appraisal Department is at 325 Swanton Way in Decatur, and the Tax Commissioner's central office is at 4380 Memorial Drive in Decatur.

sections.h2: What do transfer tax and recording involve in Stonecrest?
sections.html:
No deed is recorded in Georgia until the transfer tax is paid. The Department of Revenue states the rate as $1 for the first $1,000 or fractional part of $1,000 and 10 cents for each additional $100 or fractional part, and it makes the seller liable unless the contract says otherwise. The PT-61 declaration is filed electronically with the Georgia Superior Court Clerks' Cooperative Authority and attached to the deed at the Clerk of Superior Court.

For taxability questions, the Department of Revenue tells people to ask the Clerk of Superior Court in the county. A closing attorney or title company usually files the PT-61, pays the tax from the proceeds and records the deed.

sections.h2: What should a Stonecrest seller line up before accepting an offer?
sections.html:
1. Locate your deed, your DeKalb parcel number and the latest assessment notice.
  2. Check whether a homestead exemption is on the record, and tell the buyer it will not carry over.
  3. Look at the August tax bill and confirm which installments have been paid.
  4. Ask the mortgage servicer for a payoff statement and the closing attorney for a lien search.
  5. Compare offers on net proceeds after the transfer tax, repair credits and closing date.

faqs.a: Yes. Stonecrest became a city after a referendum on November 8, 2016 and began operations on July 10, 2017. It handles zoning, permits and business licenses, while DeKalb County bills property tax and provides public safety.

faqs.q: When are DeKalb County property tax installments due?
faqs.a: The two installments are due September 30 and November 15, and a single payment must be made by September 30. A 5 percent penalty applies to a late payment, and the postmark rules are strict.

faqs.q: Does my DeKalb homestead exemption go to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. The county brochure says exemptions are not transferable, so the buyer must apply on their own and meet the January 1 ownership and residency tests.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my DeKalb property value?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the mailing date on the assessment notice. The appeal must be hand-delivered or postmarked by that deadline, and fax or email appeals are not accepted.

faqs.q: Who is responsible for the property tax bill after I sell in Stonecrest?
faqs.a: It depends on the closing statement. DeKalb mails the bill to the January 1 owner and to the new owner, and the county tells buyers to ask the closing attorney or escrow agent who owes it. Unpaid tax stays attached to the property.
